# Declared Native Constrained Cold Starts

This provisional F07 calculation for issue #12136 reconstructs an explicitly
declared OpenSim 4.6 constrained **cold start**. It does not serialize an
arbitrary SimTK `State`, certify muscle physiology, or admit the 520-muscle
source for fitting. The implementation is
`tour_matching/native_prepared_state.py`; the native observation authority is
`native_constraint_state.py`.

## Source, State, and Constraint Contract

The declaration binds the exact entrypoint `.osim` SHA-256, every named
continuous state value, native time, each model-owned lock target, constraint
enforcement, absolute coordinate chart bounds and a residual tolerance. An
optional source chart is a declared linear form
$\ell(q)=\sum_i a_i q_i\in[\ell_-,\ell_+]$. This supports a separately
reviewed composite-coordinate rule; a matching name alone never establishes
its anatomical meaning. All angles are radians, time is seconds, and native
position/velocity errors retain their native units. The caller chooses the
tolerance from the declared source and numerical context; this method supplies
no physiological acceptance threshold.

The owned model is loaded from unchanged source bytes. OpenSim `initSystem()`
performs native initialization assembly. The preparation recipe then
temporarily unlocks each declared native locked coordinate, sets its explicit
model-owned target, relocks it, restores every named continuous state value and
sets the declared clock. It performs no further assembly or muscle
equilibration. The observer checks the achieved coordinate, lock, QErr/UErr,
constraint enforcement, chart and source hash. An optional expected audit
requires every native observation to match a separately retained producer
audit. A model-owned target is never inferred from the named coordinate value
or serialized default. The source XML is not modified.

The entrypoint XML digest does not close external assets or libraries. Named
continuous states and lock targets do not constitute full native numerical or
discrete restart state. Time-dependent forces, prescribed coordinates and
unreviewed source controllers need separate execution policies. A source
controller may be explicitly observed but cannot enter independent replay
without the exact derived-model replacement policy below.

## Restricted Time-Only Mechanical Diagnostic

For a smooth fixture with exact scalar mechanical-actuator coverage, the
caller may declare post-limit actuator controls held by native
zero-order-hold time functions. An optional single future command step must
name the same ordered channels and occur at an interior replay knot. A source controller
can enter an explicit **derived-model policy** only when the model has exactly
one reviewed `PrescribedController`, one `Constant` function and one actuator
socket. The declaration binds its original absolute path, native serialized
subtree SHA-256, scalar source command and exact actuator path. Only this
verified controller is removed from an owned fresh model before initialization.
Source XML remains unchanged; derived loaded-model identity is distinct from
the original. Any other controller, law or channel rejects. An owned
`PrescribedController` is installed before `initSystem()`, then a fresh model
integrates without state correction. At every declared knot, native controls,
constraint residuals and chart are read back. The clock must advance from the
declared initial time and the native integrator must reach each knot exactly.
The diagnostic input digest binds source, loaded model, original-controller replacement,
initial observation, actuator order, controls, knots and
Runge–Kutta–Merson accuracy. A repeated fresh run
must agree under this same policy; changing the future command must change
the native result while preserving the common sampled prefix.
The separate admission digest binds the preparation-adapter source SHA-256,
declared lock targets, coordinate and linear source charts, constraint
enforcement, residual tolerance and controller policy. Neither digest is a
complete physical-state or publication certificate.

This input player excludes muscles, non-actuator native forces and unreplaced
source controllers, including recursively discovered components outside their
registered sets. It is a mechanical software diagnostic, not a T01
muscle-excitation bundle or an all-force/contact parity claim. Source actuator
bounds and observed applied controls are checked;
native constraint reactions remain plant outputs.

## Actual Native Evidence and Remaining Gates

The analytic OpenSim fixture has a coordinate coupler $q_d=2q$ and a scalar
mechanical actuator. A locked-joint fixture proves that identical named
continuous values with a different declared model-owned lock target do not
silently pass. Wrong enforcement, wrong actuator coverage, unreviewed native
force, source mutation and chart exit also reject. The actual
`physical_humerus_v2/candidate-129.osim`
prepared receipt lies within the reviewed shoulder-elevation chart
$[0.403598785852187,0.643598785852187]$ rad, retains $r=a+b$ within its
source range, and has full-row-rank native constraint Jacobian at that state.
Its source default is outside the chart. Its sole original constant mechanical
controller is bound by subtree digest and replaced only under the declared
derived policy. Original and replacement native trajectories agree at sampled
knots in named state, derivatives, QErr/UErr, actuator control and actuation;
an owned command step after the shared prefix changes the mechanical future.
The original-controller observation
remains available and never silently invokes replacement. Knot-level chart
checks do not prove that an internal Runge–Kutta stage stayed within the chart.
This is neither source-identical native replay nor a physiological shoulder or
muscle-excitation result.

The unchanged 520-muscle source still requires approved capture registration,
marker attachment, passive-force policy, assistance exclusion, exact native
constraint/contact/grip policy and complete bounded state preparation before
a real Moco solve or excitation replay. All 17 variant rows, six engine
families and the fully muscular OpenSim endpoint remain open.
